The user wants to change their VS Code settings to auto-approve everything. They're referring to a setting that likely controls tool/action approvals, possibly for GitHub Copilot or some extension. Let me search for settings files in the workspace.The auto-approve setting you're referring to is typically in VS Code's user settings. Let me check the workspace settings file: I can see your settings file. To auto-approve all terminal commands, you need to add `"/.*/": true` to the `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` section. Let me update this: The settings file is outside the workspace. I'll open it for you in VS Code: I've opened your `settings.json` file. To auto-approve **all** terminal commands, you need to add this line to the `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` section:

```json
"/.*/": true
```

Add it as the **first item** in the `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` object, like this:

```json
"chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove": {
    "/.*/": true,
    "Test-Path": true,
    // ... rest of your existing rules
}
```

| Project | Technology | Purpose |
|---------|------------|---------|
| **workflows/** + **templates/** | Azure Logic Apps (Consumption) + ARM | Customer analysis and conversation workflows using AI/Cognitive Services. Main workspace focus. |
| **AzureWorkCLI** | Python CLI | Wrapper around Azure CLI with enhanced output formatting for resource management |
| **ccass-conversations** | Python + Dataverse | Retrieves and processes customer service conversations from Dynamics 365 |
| **contractor-portal** | HTML/CSS/JS (static) | Local web UI for contractors to manage jobs, schedules, and profiles |
| **contractor-portal-dataverse** | Node.js + Express | Backend server connecting Contractor Portal to Dynamics 365 Field Service via OAuth |
| **marc-home-assistant** | Python + REST API | Client library for controlling your Home Assistant on Raspberry Pi |
| **mcp-dataverse-server** | Python MCP Server | Model Context Protocol server enabling AI assistants to read/update Dataverse Contacts |
| **pcf-controls** | TypeScript + PCF | Power Apps Component Framework controls: FeatureTile, PCFGridMJ, YesNoTickCross |
| **Personal** | Python | Raspberry Pi GPIO and Home Assistant experimentation projects |
| **PowerPagesContosoDemo002** | Power Pages | Customer portal development for Dynamics 365 Field Service |
| **raspberry-pi** | Python + SSH | Remote management client for Raspberry Pi 5 (SSH, containers, monitoring) |

### **Recommended Additions**

#### For Azure & Logic Apps Development
| Extension | ID | Why |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| **Azure CLI Tools** | `ms-vscode.azurecli` | Syntax highlighting and IntelliSense for Azure CLI scripts |
| **ARM Template Viewer** | `bencoleman.armview` | Visual diagram of your ARM templates (azuredeploy.json) |
| **Bicep** | `ms-azuretools.vscode-bicep` | Modern ARM alternative - cleaner syntax than JSON |

#### For Python Development
| Extension | ID | Why |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| **Ruff** | `charliermarsh.ruff` | Extremely fast Python linter (replaces flake8, isort, etc.) |
| **autoDocstring** | `njpwerner.autodocstring` | Generate Python docstrings automatically |

#### For JavaScript/Node.js (contractor-portal-dataverse)
| Extension | ID | Why |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| **REST Client** | `humao.rest-client` | Test your Dataverse API calls directly from VS Code |
| **Thunder Client** | `rangav.vscode-thunder-client` | Postman-like API testing in VS Code |

#### For PCF Controls
| Extension | ID | Why |
|-----------|-----|-----|

#### For Raspberry Pi / SSH

#### For Home Assistant

|-----------|-----|-----|
| You already have `keesschollaart.vscode-home-assistant` ✓ | — | YAML autocomplete for HA configs |

#### General Productivity

| **GitLens** | `eamodio.gitlens` | Enhanced Git integration, blame annotations, history |

```json
  "textEditContent": "\"\"\"Authentication module for Dataverse using MSAL.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom msal import ConfidentialClientApplication\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\n\nclass DataverseAuth:\n    \"\"\"Handle OAuth2 authentication for Dataverse API.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        tenant_id: Optional[str] = None,\n        client_id: Optional[str] = None,\n        client_secret: Optional[str] = None,\n        base_url: Optional[str] = None,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize authentication.\n\n        Args:\n            tenant_id: Azure AD tenant ID\n            client_id: Azure AD application client ID\n            client_secret: Azure AD application client secret\n            base_url: Dataverse environment URL\n        \"\"\"\n        load_dotenv()\n\n        self.tenant_id = tenant_id or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_TENANT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.client_id = client_id or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_CLIENT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.client_secret = client_secret or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_CLIENT_SECRET\", \"\")\n        self.base_url = (base_url or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_BASE_URL\", \"\")).rstrip(\"/\")\n\n        if not all([self.tenant_id, self.client_id, self.client_secret, self.base_url]):\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"Missing required credentials. Set DATAVERSE_TENANT_ID, \"\n                \"DATAVERSE_CLIENT_ID, DATAVERSE_CLIENT_SECRET, and DATAVERSE_BASE_URL \"\n                \"environment variables or pass them as parameters.\"\n            )\n\n        self._app = ConfidentialClientApplication(\n            client_id=self.client_id,\n            client_credential=self.client_secret,\n            authority=f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{self.tenant_id}\",\n        )\n        self._token_cache: Optional[dict] = None\n\n    def get_token(self) -&gt; str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Get a valid access token, refreshing if necessary.\n\n        Returns:\n            Access token string\n        \"\"\"\n        scopes = [f\"{self.base_url}/.default\"]\n\n        # Try to get token from cache\n        result = self._app.acquire_token_silent(scopes, account=None)\n\n        if not result:\n            # No cached token, acquire new one\n            result = self._app.acquire_token_for_client(scopes=scopes)\n\n        if \"access_token\" in result:\n            return result[\"access_token\"]\n        else:\n            error = result.get(\"error_description\", result.get(\"error\", \"Unknown error\"))\n            raise RuntimeError(f\"Failed to acquire token: {error}\")\n\n    def get_headers(self) -&gt; dict[str, str]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Get HTTP headers with authorization for Dataverse API calls.\n\n        Returns:\n            Dictionary of headers\n        \"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {self.get_token()}\",\n            \"OData-MaxVersion\": \"4.0\",\n            \"OData-Version\": \"4.0\",\n            \"Accept\": \"application/json\",\n            \"Content-Type\": \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n        }\n",
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "\"\"\"Dataverse API client.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nimport httpx\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nfrom .auth import DataverseAuth\nfrom .entities import Case, Subject, Contact, Account\n\n\nclass DataverseClient:\n    \"\"\"Client for interacting with Microsoft Dataverse / Dynamics 365 API.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        base_url: Optional[str] = None,\n        tenant_id: Optional[str] = None,\n        client_id: Optional[str] = None,\n        client_secret: Optional[str] = None,\n        api_version: Optional[str] = None,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize the Dataverse client.\n\n        Args:\n            base_url: Dataverse environment URL\n            tenant_id: Azure AD tenant ID\n            client_id: Azure AD application client ID\n            client_secret: Azure AD application client secret\n            api_version: API version (default: v9.2)\n        \"\"\"\n        load_dotenv()\n\n        self.base_url = (base_url or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_BASE_URL\", \"\")).rstrip(\"/\")\n        self.api_version = api_version or os.getenv(\"DATAVERSE_API_VERSION\", \"v9.2\")\n\n        self._auth = DataverseAuth(\n            tenant_id=tenant_id,\n            client_id=client_id,\n            client_secret=client_secret,\n            base_url=self.base_url,\n        )\n\n        self._http_client: Optional[httpx.Client] = None\n\n    @property\n    def api_url(self) -&gt; list[Subject]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Get subject records.\n\n        Args:\n            parent_id: Filter by parent subject ID\n\n        Returns:\n            List of Subject objects\n        \"\"\"\n        filter_expr = None\n        if parent_id:\n            filter_expr = f\"_parentsubject_value eq {parent_id}\"\n\n        records = self.query(\n            entity_set=\"subjects\",\n            select=[\"subjectid\", \"title\", \"description\", \"_parentsubject_value\"],\n            filter=filter_expr,\n            orderby=\"title\",\n        )\n\n        return [Subject.from_dict(r) for r in records]\n\n    def get_subject(self, subject_id: str) -&gt; table.add_column(\"Priority\", style=\"yellow\")\n    table.add_column(\"Status\", style=\"green\")\n    table.add_column(\"Created\", style=\"dim\")\n\n    for case in cases:\n        priority_style = {\"High\": \"red\", \"Normal\": \"yellow\", \"Low\": \"dim\"}.get(case.priority, \"white\")\n        status_style = {\"Active\": \"green\", \"Resolved\": \"blue\", \"Cancelled\": \"dim\"}.get(case.state, \"white\")\n\n        table.add_row(\n            case.ticket_number,\n            case.title[:50] + \"...\" if len(case.title) &gt; 50 else case.title,\n            f\"[{priority_style}]{case.priority}[/]\",\n            f\"[{status_style}]{case.state}[/]\",\n            case.created_on.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\") if case.created_on else \"\",\n        )\n\n    console.print(table)\n\n\ndef display_subjects(client: DataverseClient, args):\n    \"\"\"Display subjects in a table.\"\"\"\n    subjects = client.get_subjects()\n\n    table = style=\"dim\")\n\n    for subject in subjects:\n        table.add_row(\n            subject.title,\n            (subject.description[:40] + \"...\") if subject.description and len(subject.description) &gt; 40 else (subject.description or \"\"),\n            \"Yes\" if subject.parent_id else \"No\",\n        )\n\n    console.print(table)\n\n\ndef display_contacts(client: DataverseClient, args):\n    \"\"\"Display contacts in a table.\"\"\"\n    contacts = client.get_contacts(top=args.top, search=args.search)\n\n    table = Table(title=f\"Contacts ({len(contacts)} records)\")\n    table.add_column(\"Name\", style=\"cyan\")\n    table.add_column(\"Email\", style=\"white\")\n    table.add_column(\"Phone\", style=\"dim\")\n    table.add_column(\"Job Title\", style=\"yellow\")\n\n    for contact in contacts:\n        table.add_row(\n            contact.full_name,\n            contact.email or \"\",\n            contact.phone or \"\",\n            contact.job_title or \"\",\n        )\n\n    console.print(table)\n\n\ndef display_accounts(client: DataverseClient, args):\n    \"\"\"Display accounts in a table.\"\"\"\n    accounts = client.get_accounts(top=args.top, search=args.search)\n\n    table = Table(title=f\"Accounts ({len(accounts)} records)\")\n    table.add_column(\"Name\", style=\"cyan\")\n    table.add_column(\"Email\", style=\"white\")\n    table.add_column(\"Phone\", style=\"dim\")\n    table.add_column(\"Location\", style=\"yellow\")\n\n    for account in accounts:\n        location = f\"{account.city or ''}, {account.country or   "textEditContent": "# PowerPlatform\n\nA Python client library for querying and managing data in Microsoft Dataverse / Dynamics 365.\n\n## Features\n\n- 🔐 **OAuth2 Authentication** - Client credentials flow with MSAL\n- 📊 **Entity Support** - Cases, Subjects, Contacts, Accounts\n- 🔍 **Flexible Queries** - OData filtering, selecting, ordering\n- ✏️ **CRUD Operations** - Create, Read, Update, Delete records\n- 🎨 **Rich CLI** - Beautiful table output with Rich library\n\n## Environment\n\n- **Tenant**: D365DemoTSCE63319057.onmicrosoft.com\n- **Environment**: MJCC2024\n- **URL**: https://org6cb3e9fb.crm4.dynamics.com\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Install the package:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   cd PowerPlatform\n   pip install -e .\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. The &#96;.env&#96; file is pre-configured with your Dataverse credentials.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Command Line\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# List cases\npowerplatform cases\npowerplatform cases --top 20\npowerplatform cases --status active\n\n# List subjects\npowerplatform subjects\n\n# List contacts\npowerplatform contacts\npowerplatform contacts --search \"John\"\n\n# List accounts\npowerplatform accounts\npowerplatform accounts --search \"Contoso\"\n\n# Create a case\npowerplatform create-case --title \"New Issue\" --customer &lt;contact-id&gt; --priority 1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Python API\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom powerplatform import DataverseClient\n\n# Connect to Dataverse\nwith DataverseClient() as client:\n    # Get cases\n    cases = client.get_cases(top=10, status=\"active\")\n    for case in cases:\n        print(f\"{case.ticket_number}: {case.title} ({case.priority})\")\n\n    # Get subjects\n    subjects = client.get_subjects()\n    for subject in subjects:\n        print(f\"- {subject.title}\")\n\n    # Get contacts\n    contacts = client.get_contacts(search=\"John\")\n    for contact in contacts:\n        print(f\"{contact.full_name}: {contact.email}\")\n\n    # Create a case\n    case_id = client.create_case(\n        title=\"Network connectivity issue\",\n        customer_id=\"contact-guid-here\",\n        description=\"User cannot connect to VPN\",\n        priority=1,  # High\n    )\n    print(f\"Created case: {case_id}\")\n\n    # Update a case\n    client.update_case(case_id, title=\"Updated title\")\n\n    # Generic query\n    records = client.query(\n        entity_set=\"incidents\",\n        select=[\"title\", \"ticketnumber\"],\n        filter=\"statecode eq 0\",\n        orderby=\"createdon desc\",\n        top=5,\n    )\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supported Entities\n\n| Entity | Entity Set | Methods |\n|--------|------------|---------|\n| Case | &#96;incidents&#96; | &#96;get_cases()&#96;, &#96;get_case()&#96;, &#96;create_case()&#96;, &#96;update_case()&#96; |\n| Subject | &#96;subjects&#96; | &#96;get_subjects()&#96;, &#96;get_subject()&#96; |\n| Contact | &#96;contacts&#96; | &#96;get_contacts()&#96;, &#96;get_contact()&#96;, &#96;create_contact()&#96; |\n| Account | &#96;accounts&#96; | &#96;get_accounts()&#96;, &#96;get_account()&#96; |\n\n## Adding New Entities\n\n1. Add a dataclass in &#96;entities.py&#96;\n2. Add query methods in &#96;client.py&#96;\n3. Add CLI commands in &#96;__main__.py&#96;\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPowerPlatform/\n├── pyproject.toml\n├── README.md\n├── .env                    # Your credentials (gitignored)\n├── .env.example\n└── src/\n    └── powerplatform/\n        ├── __init__.py\n        ├── __main__.py     # CLI entry point\n        ├── auth.py         # OAuth2 authentication\n        ├── client.py       # Dataverse API client\n        └── entities.py     # Entity models\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n",
```

## Project Summary

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `client.py` | Main Dataverse API client |

## Usage

**Command Line:**
```powershell
powerplatform cases                    # List cases
powerplatform cases --status active    # Filter by status
powerplatform subjects                 # List subjects
powerplatform contacts --search "John" # Search contacts
powerplatform accounts                 # List accounts
```

**Python API:**
```python
from powerplatform import DataverseClient

with DataverseClient() as client:
    cases = client.get_cases(top=10, status="active")
    subjects = client.get_subjects()
    
    # Create a case
    case_id = client.create_case(
        title="New issue",
        customer_id="contact-guid",
        priority=1,  # High
    )
```
